title: Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management: automatic preservation of deleted content for high-risk users
summary: The briefing matches the roadmap and Microsoft's preview documentation, including the 120-day preservation period, controls, audit events and storage implications. It appropriately distinguishes the planned general availability release from the preview and reports the conflicting setup instructions without choosing one.

claims.claim: The planned Data Lifecycle Management integration automatically applies retention labels to preserve deleted emails and files based on insider risk.
claims.quote: The integration with Data Lifecycle Management will automatically apply retention labels to preserve deleted emails and files based on a user’s insider risk level.

claims.claim: Adaptive Protection moves users in and out of policies as their insider risk levels change.
claims.quote: automatically moving users in and out of policies as their risk levels change over time

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; Risk assessment; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Automatic preservation targets deletions by users assigned the Elevated insider risk level.
claims.quote: Preserve any SharePoint, OneDrive, or Exchange Online content deleted by a risky user for 120 days. A risky user in this case is a user that Adaptive Protection assigns the Elevated risk level.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; Risk assessment
claims.claim: The integration covers deleted content in SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange.
claims.quote: If these users delete content from SharePoint, OneDrive, or Exchange, a retention label is automatically applied to that content to retain it for 120 days.

claims.claim: Users do not see the retention label.
claims.quote: Unlike other labeling scenarios, users don't see the retention label

claims.claim: Items become eligible for permanent deletion after the 120-day period expires.
claims.quote: After the 120 days expire, the items then become eligible for permanent deletion.
